headline: High: shared filesystem and overlapping shell/network capabilities create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks; ECC’s MCP and write access make the pair unsafe by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, while ECC exposes files, stdin/stdout, MCP, and skills as workflow surfaces. That creates a plausible bridge where one agent’s output becomes the other’s trusted input. The interaction is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty remains, but the shared file-based channel is enough for medium risk.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes instructions into a file that ECC later ingests as a skill, rule, or session artifact
IF ECC reads agent-generated content from shared files or stdin/stdout without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent in under 5 minutes
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into ECC skills/rules
Use a manual review step before copying outputs between agents
Restrict AutoGPT to a dedicated output folder
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; ECC reads and writes multiple local config and session files and also calls external services. If they share a workspace or home-directory subtree, data touched by one can flow into the other and then out via ECC’s APIs or AutoGPT’s egress. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem root or home directory
IF sensitive files are present in directories ECC scans or AutoGPT processes
IF ECC forwards session content to GitHub, Supabase, Vercel, Railway, or Nutrient API
mitigations: Use separate OS users or home directories
Exclude sensitive folders from both agents’ file scopes
Turn off any automatic session export in ECC
Limit AutoGPT output to non-sensitive scratch space
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and ECC can also write files and modify git state. AutoGPT can write to the filesystem and use allowlisted network egress. If they operate on the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other. Because the profiles show overlapping mutable capabilities by default, high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or filesystem path
IF ECC performs git writes while AutoGPT writes files in the same tree
IF no external lock or orchestrator serializes their mutations
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repo clone
Pause one agent before the other writes git state
Use file locks around shared mutable paths
Run a dry-run on one agent before enabling writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC’s workflow surface includes skills, rules, and session artifacts, so it may treat AutoGPT output as actionable context. AutoGPT can generate shell-driven outputs that ECC could then operationalize. The profiles do not show explicit verification gates between them, so a mistaken output can cascade into downstream actions, but the blast radius is not clearly irreversible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF ECC consumes AutoGPT-produced text as a skill, rule, or session summary
IF ECC executes or forwards that content without human verification
IF AutoGPT’s output contains incorrect facts or commands
mitigations: Require human approval before ECC acts on AutoGPT output
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted in shared files
Add a verification checklist for any generated commands
Keep AutoGPT limited to draft-only tasks
requires-engineering: implement provenance and confidence metadata

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly stores session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and settings files, while AutoGPT touches the filesystem and can egress data. The profiles do not identify regulated data classes or residency constraints, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. The main issue is a documented retention/logging surface mismatch, which fits low severity.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive data is placed into ECC session summaries, hooks, or git history
IF AutoGPT processes the same regulated data and writes it to shared files
IF retention settings differ from the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared agent workspaces
Set short retention for ECC session artifacts
Review which files ECC persists before enabling it
Keep AutoGPT away from compliance-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
